# Deployment & Prerequisites

## Platform Requirements

ZTWIM requires OpenShift v4.19+ for development builds [5] and v4.20+ for GA
installations via the stable-v1 channel [22]. The product was available as a
technology preview in OpenShift 4.18-4.19 [35] before reaching general
availability on January 23, 2026 [2].

Installation is performed via OperatorHub (web console) or CLI [22]. ZTWIM is a
Day-2 operator and is not part of the base OpenShift install [5].

## Namespace and Permissions

The operator deploys into the `zero-trust-workload-identity-manager` namespace
and ignores `openshift-*` namespaces for workload identity assignment [12][22].
Cluster-admin privileges are required for installation [22].

## Storage and Infrastructure

A minimum of 1Gi persistent volume is required for the SPIRE Server [22]. For
production high-availability deployments, PostgreSQL is the recommended
datastore (SQLite is the default but not recommended for production) [2].

## Development Environment

Building from source requires Go 1.23.0+, Docker 17.03+, and kubectl v1.11.3+
[5].

## Deployed Components

The operator manages five components: SPIRE Server, SPIRE Agent, SPIFFE CSI
Driver, OIDC Discovery Provider, and the Controller Manager [5].

## Resource Footprint

The SPIRE sizing table from the upstream documentation covers deployments from
10 to 10,000 workloads across 10 to 5,000 agents [10].

EdgeX Foundry measurements provide concrete resource numbers: SPIRE Server
requires 151 MB disk and 30 MB RAM; SPIRE Agent requires 114 MB disk and 64 MB
RAM per node [29].

## Gaps and Limitations

1. The HPE SPIRE operator (a prior art reference) was characterized as a
   "proof-of-concept by interns," illustrating the difficulty of building
   production-grade SPIRE operators.
2. CPU spikes to 150-160% have been documented in the SPIRE issue tracker [25].
3. Agent memory leaks reaching 3.5GB have been reported [25].
4. Agent CPU consumption ranges from 390m to 634m cores under load, scaling
   linearly with workload count [25].
